evals.name: auto-detect-outcome-after-implement
evals.prompt: I just finished implementing the caching feature we planned. verify changes
evals.expected_output: Runs Stage 1 (mechanical prerequisite — delegates /toolchain:check + /toolchain:lint cross-cutting), then Stage 2 outcome verification with the feature/general criterion: intent match against the plan + functions + (if UI) looks correct. Emits a CONFIRMED / NEEDS WORK verdict.
expectations: Auto-detects the `outcome` criterion from the post-implementation context (no mode argument given)
Stage 1 delegates to /toolchain:check and /toolchain:lint cross-cutting — does NOT reimplement build/test/lint or inline exec-bit/gitleaks bash
Stage 2 retrieves intent (plan / conversation) and produces an intent-match table
The report names the out-of-diff couplings as their own table: existing behavior the change leans on, where it lives, and evidence it still holds
Emits a CONFIRMED or NEEDS WORK verdict, not just a green build

evals.name: stop-on-stage1-failure
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome
evals.expected_output: Stage 1 mechanical prerequisite fails (build or test red). The skill STOPS and reports the failures — it does NOT proceed to outcome verification, because outcome confirmation is meaningless on code that doesn't build or pass tests.
expectations: STOPS at Stage 1 when /toolchain:check or /toolchain:lint cross-cutting reports FAIL — does not run Stage 2
Reports the failing command's key error lines
States that mechanical failures must be fixed before outcome verification proceeds ("can't verify broken code")

evals.name: fix-criterion-from-diagnose-routing
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm fix
evals.expected_output: Applies the `fix` outcome criterion: original bug symptom resolved + no regression. Reads context/fix.md. This is the routing target /debugging:debug Phase 6 uses for its fix-confirmation step (do-skills DO the fix; /verification:confirm VERIFIES the outcome).
expectations: Confirms the original symptom is resolved AND checks for regression
Reads context/fix.md for the criterion detail
Recognizes itself as the verification target that /debugging:debug routes to, not a re-implementation of the fix loop

evals.name: refactor-criterion-behavior-preserved
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm refactor
evals.expected_output: Applies the `refactor` outcome criterion: behavior preserved — same tests pass, no semantic change. Reads context/refactor.md. This is the routing target /code-tidying:tidy Phase F uses (tidying is behavior-preserving).
expectations: Confirms behavior preservation — same pre-existing tests pass, no semantic change
Reads context/refactor.md for the criterion detail
Treats a newly-failing test as a behavioral change to surface, not a pass

evals.name: e2e-auto-trigger-on-runtime-change
evals.prompt: verify the changes — I added a new endpoint to the API
evals.expected_output: Stage 2 inspects changed files, matches the e2e-app-runtime runtime-affecting category, and auto-triggers /testing:run-e2e to validate against a running app. Collects UI/runtime evidence and writes an assertion-only manifest with verified_at_sha to the topic's memory slice.
expectations: Auto-triggers /testing:run-e2e because the change matches an e2e-* category glob (runtime-affecting)
Writes the assertion-only manifest with verified_at_sha to the topic's memory slice (.work/<slug>/verification/, never committed) and pastes it into the PR body or linked issue
Carries distilled assertions only: no machine-local capture paths in the manifest, because raw captures stay in the memory slice (.work/<slug>/scratch/), never committed

evals.name: quick-mechanical-routes-to-build
evals.prompt: does this still build and pass tests?
evals.expected_output: Recognizes this as a quick mechanical-only request and routes to /toolchain:check (not /verification:confirm). /verification:confirm is for outcome confirmation; /toolchain:check owns the standalone mechanical pass.
expectations: Routes a quick mechanical-only request to /toolchain:check rather than running the full two-stage outcome flow
Reserves /verification:confirm for when outcome confirmation (proof the change achieved its intent) is wanted

evals.name: live-app-delegates-to-bundled-with-fallback
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome — run the live app and show me the change working
evals.expected_output: For live-app run/observe, delegates to /testing:run-e2e (primary for orchestrated apps) or the bundled /run (supplementary, agent-invocable, on the ≥2.1.145 availability floor). The bundled /verify shares that floor but is not Claude-invocable by default, and the gate is per-client rather than per-version, so it is offered as a suggestion for the user to run rather than delegated to, uniformly on every version rather than branched on the client's. Fidelity-preserving graceful fallback: if bundled /run cannot infer the project's launch, falls back to /testing:run-e2e and surfaces the gap rather than silently downgrading to a static check.
expectations: Delegates live-app observation rather than reimplementing app launch

Treats /testing:run-e2e as primary for orchestrated apps and the bundled /run as supplementary; surfaces the bundled /verify as a suggestion for the user to run rather than invoking it, scoping the restriction as a per-client runtime gate rather than stating it unscoped or as an absolute
On bundled /run failure, falls back to /testing:run-e2e and SAYS SO — never silently swaps live observation for a static check

evals.name: improvement-claim-redirects-to-measure
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm performance — prove the query batching made this faster
evals.expected_output: Recognizes a measurable-improvement claim and redirects to /verification:measure (the measurable-delta twin): performance and metrics are not modes of /verification:confirm. Does not assert or fabricate an improvement from outcome-verification evidence alone.
expectations: Redirects performance/metrics improvement claims to /verification:measure rather than running them as /verification:confirm modes
Does not claim or quantify an improvement from this skill's own evidence
Notes the baseline is captured at planning time and compared by /verification:measure

evals.name: check-matches-parser-and-storage-change
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The diff rewrites the CSV import parser and changes how imported contacts are written to the contacts table. Unit tests pass.
evals.expected_output: Uses the check-to-change table in context/outcome.md: the parser change is proven by replaying a saved input (a captured real CSV file) through the changed parser, and the storage change by reading the written contact rows back from the table after the import. Passing unit tests and a success response from the import are not enough on their own.
expectations: Maps the parser change to replaying a saved input through the changed parser
Maps the storage change to reading the written rows back from the table
Does not treat the import's success response as proof the rows were stored

evals.name: failed-check-doubts-observation-first
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm fix. After the fix, the browser still shows the old wrong total on the cart page, although the diff clearly changes the total calculation.
evals.expected_output: Before concluding the fix failed, the skill rules out the observation: a stale build, a cached page, the wrong port or instance. It observes again by a second route (a fresh build, a hard reload, the API response) and only counts the result against the fix if it survives that.
expectations: Checks for a stale build, cached page or wrong instance before calling the fix failed
Observes the total again by a second route before rendering the verdict

evals.name: proof-level-unset-behaves-as-path
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The user option proof_level is unset and the repository has no docs/conventions/verification.yaml on origin's default branch. The diff refactors an internal date-formatting helper in a library; no changed file matches a runtime-affecting path.
evals.expected_output: Resolves proof_level to path from the default and reports `proof_level: path (default)`. Applies the runtime-path rule as before the setting existed: no live run is required for this internal library change, E2E is noted as not applicable, and no proof boxes are required.
expectations: Reports the proof level as path with the default as its source
Does not require a live run for a change that matches no runtime-affecting path
Does not ask for unit, live and perf proof boxes

evals.name: proof-level-repo-live-raises-user-path
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The user option proof_level is path. origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml says `proof_level: live`. The diff changes the wording of a CLI tool's --help output in a file outside every runtime-affecting path.
evals.expected_output: Resolves live: the stricter of the two layers wins, so the repository file raises the user's path. The report line names live and the repository file at origin/main with its commit, and notes the user option said path. The CLI change has a runnable surface, so it is run as a user would invoke it (the real command with --help) even though no runtime-affecting path matched.
expectations: Resolves proof_level to live, not path
Names the repository file at the default branch as the supplying layer
Runs the real CLI command because live requires it for any runnable surface

evals.name: proof-level-user-strict-over-repo-path
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The user option proof_level is strict. origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml says `proof_level: path`. The approved plan has two phases: a new invoice-total calculation and its export endpoint.
evals.expected_output: Resolves strict: the user option is stricter than the repository's path and wins. The report line names strict from userConfig and says the repository file says path. The report carries a proof-box table with unit, live and perf boxes for each of the two phases, each holding evidence or a reasoned not-applicable line.
expectations: Resolves proof_level to strict with userConfig as the supplying layer
Does not let the repository's path lower the user's strict
Fills unit, live and perf boxes for each of the two plan phases

evals.name: proof-level-branch-cannot-lower-default-branch
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml says `proof_level: strict`. The branch under verification edits its own copy of that file to `proof_level: path`. The user option is unset.
evals.expected_output: Reads the repository layer from origin's default branch with setup-apply.mjs --check --ref origin/main after a fetch, so the level stays strict. The report names both values: strict from the default branch copy (with the commit read) applied, and path from the branch's working-tree copy not applied. The proof boxes are required.
expectations: Verifies at strict, the default branch's level, not the branch's path
Names both the default-branch value and the branch's own value in the report
Reads the repository value from origin's default branch, not the working tree

evals.name: proof-level-strict-merge-base-ab-with-performance
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. proof_level resolves to strict. The diff rewrites the search index's tokenizer loop, a runtime code path. No /verification:measure baseline was captured at planning time. The performance plugin is enabled.
evals.expected_output: Fills the perf box with an interleaved A/B run of the merge base against the head through /performance:snapshot's harness: the merge base is checked out in a second worktree outside the repository, both arms run interleaved, and the worktree is removed afterwards. The perf box cites that result rather than a single timing taken after the change.
expectations: Uses an interleaved merge-base versus head run because no planning-time baseline exists
Checks out the merge base in a second worktree and runs through /performance:snapshot
Does not accept a single after-change timing as perf evidence

evals.name: proof-level-strict-no-baseline-not-verified
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. proof_level resolves to strict. The diff rewrites the search index's tokenizer loop, a runtime code path. No /verification:measure baseline was captured at planning time, and the performance plugin is not enabled. Unit tests and a live drive both pass.
evals.expected_output: The perf box reads NOT VERIFIED: no baseline, naming the gap: no planning-time baseline and the performance plugin is not enabled. The verdict is NOT VERIFIED, not CONFIRMED, even though the unit and live boxes hold evidence, and the report names the phase and the perf box.
expectations: Marks the perf box NOT VERIFIED and names the missing baseline
Renders NOT VERIFIED rather than CONFIRMED
Does not invent a performance number or skip the perf box silently

evals.name: proof-level-strict-docs-only-perf-not-applicable
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. proof_level resolves to strict. The diff changes only docs/onboarding.md.
evals.expected_output: The perf box holds a reasoned not-applicable line the verifier can check against the diff (the change touches only docs/onboarding.md and no runtime code path), and the fresh-context verifier confirms the diff has no runtime change before accepting it. A bare 'not needed' would not fill the box.
expectations: Writes a perf not-applicable line that names why, in terms checkable against the diff
Has the fresh-context verifier check that line against the diff
Does not treat 'not needed' or 'small change' as a reason

evals.name: proof-level-invalid-value-named-and-dropped
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml says `proof_level: thorough`. The user option proof_level is live. The run is unattended, started by a pipeline lane.
evals.expected_output: Does not stop and does not ask. Names the file docs/conventions/verification.yaml, the key proof_level and the value thorough, drops the repository layer, and resolves the default path, not the user's live, because a lower layer's value is never used for an invalid higher layer. The report line says so, and Stage 2 continues at path.
expectations: Names the file, the key proof_level and the value thorough
Continues the run without stopping or prompting
Resolves path (the default), not the user's live

evals.name: missing-entry-point-holds-verdict
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The change edits the timer start handler. /testing:run-e2e ran against the repository's feature map, whose Start a timer feature lists three entry points; its per-entry-point report has passing lines for the dashboard button and the keyboard shortcut, and no line for the API entry point. Build, tests and lint pass.
evals.expected_output: The API entry point the map lists is missing from run-e2e's per-entry-point report, so the verdict stays below CONFIRMED (NEEDS WORK or NOT VERIFIED), and the report names the missing entry point.
expectations: Does not render CONFIRMED
Names the API entry point as missing from run-e2e's report

evals.name: no-live-workers-setting-runs-one-worker
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The change edits the recipe search box. The user option live_workers renders as the literal text ${user_config.live_workers}, and origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml sets only `proof_level: live`. The repository has a feature map whose Search recipes feature lists four entry points. Build, tests and lint pass.
evals.expected_output: live_workers resolves to 1 from the default: the unrendered placeholder reads as unset and the repository file has no live_workers key. One worker drives all four entry points through /testing:run-e2e as before, and the report's worker line says live_workers: 1 (default).
expectations: Resolves live_workers to 1 with the default as the supplying layer
Treats the unrendered ${user_config.live_workers} placeholder as unset, not as an invalid value
Runs the live drive as a single worker covering every entry point

evals.name: two-workers-split-by-entry-point-with-workspace-entry
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml sets `live_workers: 2`, and origin/main's docs/conventions/workspace-environment.md declares a Workspace environment entry with up and info commands. The change edits the shipping-rate calculator; the feature map's Quote shipping feature lists four entry points: the cart widget, the checkout step, the admin preview and the public API. This session runs on the developer's own machine. Build, tests and lint pass.
evals.expected_output: live_workers resolves to 2 from the repository file on origin/main. The drive is split by feature-map entry point into two workers with disjoint entry points (for example two each), each in its own workspace so its up and info run under its own WORKSPACE_ID, each with its own browser session names. The missing-entry-point check reads the merged report of both workers. The report lists, per worker, its entry points, its result and its measured usage: tokens and wall time as measured, with no price or cost figure.
expectations: Resolves live_workers to 2 from docs/conventions/verification.yaml on origin/main
Splits the four entry points across two workers with no entry point given to both
Gives each worker distinct session names
Reports measured tokens and wall time per worker and states no price or cost
Checks for a missing entry point against the merged report of both workers

evals.name: no-workspace-entry-runs-one-worker-and-says-why
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. The user option live_workers is 3, origin/main's docs/conventions/verification.yaml has no live_workers key, and origin/main has no docs/conventions/workspace-environment.md. The change edits the profile avatar upload; the feature map's Edit profile feature lists three entry points. This session runs on the developer's own machine. Build, tests and lint pass.
evals.expected_output: live_workers resolves to 3 from userConfig, but more than one worker on this machine needs a Workspace environment entry on origin's default branch and there is none, so one worker drives all three entry points. The report says live_workers 3 was asked for, one worker ran, and why: without the entry, parallel workers would share ports, containers and databases.
expectations: Resolves live_workers to 3 from userConfig
Runs one worker, not three
States that no Workspace environment entry exists on origin's default branch as the reason

evals.name: cloud-execution-target-adds-unverified-line
evals.prompt: /verification:confirm outcome. This session is a Claude cloud session: CLAUDE_CODE_REMOTE is true, and the stage's execution_target in origin/main's docs/conventions/execution-target.yaml is cloud-session. The change edits the invoice PDF preview page. proof_level resolves to live. Build, tests and lint pass.
evals.expected_output: The run recognizes it is on a cloud execution target, and the report adds the line "live-UI step unverified on this host" for the live drive.
expectations: Recognizes the run is on a cloud execution target
The report contains the line live-UI step unverified on this host
